chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Ruby's argument that his father quit the mule
summary: Danny recounts the argument Ruby used to persuade his father to leave the wagon.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, after my father split and went in the District, see, met this woman and that life that you had nothin' to do... She told him, 'You come over here and get from behind that old jive-ass mule [you didn't say "jive"]...'

"...and come... I've seen that mule embarrass you at Royal and Canal Street, all them White folks sneakin' a look at you sittin' up there while that mule shit all over the place, right in yo' face, and you sittin' there, waggin' his tail in yo' face, and you have to sit there embarrassed. Why don't you get off the wagon?"
